description: We are a team of students from UTAS Salalah interested in technology, innovation, and creative problem-solving. We are excited to work together, learn new skills, and create an innovative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: What if the machines we erased from our memory could tell us their stories? Many school students find space exploration overwhelming and passive, so they never realize today’s missions stand on machines that paved the way before them. Between Dust and Stars solves this in a new way: a bored student wakes up on Mars beside a robotic companion, and players investigate clues and solve mission-inspired puzzles to awaken forgotten NASA spacecraft, revealing their real stories. Addressing the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge, we turn passive learning into active discovery.
details:
Between Dust and Stars is a browser-based animated adventure for school students. The story begins in an ordinary classroom, where a bored student falls asleep and awakens on Mars beside a mysterious, lively robotic companion.

Together they find silent spacecraft left behind after their missions. But these machines won’t talk to just anyone. To earn their stories, players must discover what lies around them, investigate the clues scattered in the dust, awaken each sleeping machine by solving puzzles inspired by its real mission, and finally remember, as it shares its true discoveries, struggles, and legacy through an animated flashback in a voice all its own.

We drew on NASA’s open data and official sources for every mission detail, then turned them into simple clues, puzzles, and short stories that students can easily understand, while the dialogue and personalities are imagined to keep the experience engaging.

The encounters form one continuous story that ends with a final mystery: the companion’s own forgotten story. After each story, students can also write a message to the forgotten machine, to thank it, ask it a question, or share what they learned, so that the machines are no longer forgotten but remembered. Through the game, students come to understand the importance of these machines and realize that they opened the way for every mission that followed.

💻 Tech Stack

Frontend: HTML5, CSS, React, TypeScript

Backend: Python

Database: MongoDB

Responsive Web Layout (runs in any browser, no special hardware)

Watercolor storybook illustrations and animated scenes

Deployed online as a public web app [hosting platform, e.g., Emergent]

✨ Innovation Highlights

📖 Narrative Design: One continuous story connects forgotten missions, ending with the companion’s own hidden story.

🔍 Learning by Discovery: Students investigate clues and solve mission-inspired puzzles to awaken each machine and unlock its story.

🎨 Visual Storytelling: Watercolor illustrations and animated flashbacks make space history warm and memorable for young learners.

📡 Data Trust: Mission information sourced from NASA’s open data and official sources.

💻 AI tools/software:

ChatGPT: helped us analyze and organize NASA mission data.

Claude: translated the story’s dialogue into English.

Emergent: used to generate the website’s code.
